channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Families of Soldiers Killed in Caspian Sea Sign Non-Disclosure Agreements on Compensation
item.description: Families of military personnel who perished in the Caspian Sea incident have signed documents agreeing not to disclose details about the compensation they received. This move suggests a desire for privacy or a structured approach to managing the aftermath of the tragedy.

item.title: Traffic Accidents in Logar Province Claim Three Lives, Injure Seven
item.description: Sources in Logar province report that at least three people were killed and seven injured in five traffic accidents over the past 24 hours. The Taliban's provincial police command confirmed incidents resulting in four deaths and 17 injuries from 11 accidents in the past week. Driver negligence and excessive speed were cited as primary causes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Exports of Copper, Tantalum to US, Japan, Thailand
item.description: Kazakhstan's exports of refined copper and unwrought lead have increased in January-July 2026. The country exported 278.6 thousand tons of copper, earning $3.4 billion, with Turkey as the main buyer. Tantalum exports also rose significantly, with the US being the largest purchaser. Zinc exports, however, saw a decline.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands International Cooperation in Higher Education
item.description: Kazakhstan is strengthening its position in the global education space by expanding international cooperation in higher education. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education reports that 33 foreign university branches operate in the country, and 131 Kazakh universities collaborate with institutions in 24 countries on dual-degree programs. This initiative aims to provide international-level education to Kazakh youth.

item.title: Pakistan Rebukes Taliban on Women's Rights, Citing Their Own Record
item.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting responded to Taliban spokesperson's remarks, stating the group should not lecture others on governance and citizenship rights given their treatment of women. The ministry accused the Taliban of deflecting from terrorism threats originating from Afghanistan and failing to uphold commitments against using Afghan soil for attacks on Pakistan.

item.title: Yale Graduate's Research on Child Diarrhea Wins Health Equity Award
item.description: Madi Baltagolov, a graduate of Yale School of Public Health, received an award for best master's thesis in health equity. His research analyzed data from 51 countries to create a statistical model predicting healthcare seeking behavior for child diarrhea in low- and middle-income nations. The study aims to reduce preventable child mortality.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Challenges Selling Saiga Meat Despite Population Growth
item.description: Despite a significant increase in the saiga population in Kazakhstan, reaching over 4.5 million, selling their meat has become difficult. Although hunting quotas were set, demand has decreased after initial interest, leading to stockpiled meat. The Ministry of Trade is negotiating with retailers to make saiga meat more accessible and expand sales channels.

item.title: Kazakhstan National University of Sports Launches Esports Educational Program
item.description: The Kazakhstan National University of Sports has admitted its first students to an 'Esports (Esport)' educational program. This initiative addresses the growing esports industry, which is projected to reach 640 million global viewers by 2025, with Kazakhstan's audience potentially hitting 5 million this year. The program aims to train professionals for organizing tournaments and teams.

item.title: Tajikistan to Build and Renovate 13 Schools in Sughd and Khatlon Regions with Kuwaiti Loan
item.description: Thirteen schools in Tajikistan's Sughd and Khatlon regions will be built and renovated using a $20 million concessional loan from the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development. The Ministry of Finance confirmed the agreement, stating the project aims to improve general education and accommodate a growing number of students. Construction and renovation are scheduled from 2026 to 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks Alternatives to Yandex Ride-Sharing Service After Outage
item.description: Following a disruption of the Yandex ride-sharing service on October 11, Kazakhstan is exploring alternatives. Services like inDrive, Aparu, and Tez Taxi are available, with inDrive seeing increased demand. However, some users reported higher fares on inDrive. While inDrive has a significant operational center in Kazakhstan, it was founded in Yakutsk and is registered in the US.

item.title: Kazakhstan's eGov platform to be upgraded to 'eGov 3.0' with AI integration
item.description: Kazakhstan's electronic government portal, eGov, is set to be upgraded to 'eGov 3.0', aiming to simplify digital services. The new model will proactively identify user needs and automate processes. Developed on the 'QazTech' platform, it will leverage artificial intelligence to adapt services to citizen demands, rather than the other way around.

item.title: Kazakh startup Factory Builder AI offers digital modeling to reduce industrial costs
item.description: Kazakh startup Factory Builder AI proposes using digital models to simulate and test future production facilities before construction. This approach allows for the identification of potential bottlenecks, equipment limitations, or resource shortages that could arise from production increases, thus preventing costly on-site modifications and optimizing efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Sign Cooperation Roadmap Until 2029
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium have signed a roadmap for cooperation between their foreign ministries for 2027-2029. The document, signed during the Belgian King's state visit, aims to enhance political dialogue, regular consultations, and joint initiatives. Discussions also covered visa facilitation and readmission agreements.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Online Ambulance Tracking and New Medical Aid Rules from October 13
item.description: Starting October 13, Kazakhstan will introduce new regulations for emergency medical services and air ambulance. These changes include automatic notifications for ambulance dispatch, real-time online tracking of their movement, and equipping medical personnel with video badges. The exact launch dates for these features in each region are not specified in the order.

item.title: Businesswoman on Trial in Karaganda for Allegedly Defrauding Over 500 People of Nearly $220 Million
item.description: A businesswoman in Karaganda is on trial for allegedly defrauding over 500 people of approximately one billion tenge (about $220 million) by promising to deliver goods from China at low prices. She accepted orders and prepayments nationwide via messengers, advertising through bloggers. Only the first clients received their orders; others have waited for two years.

item.title: Trump Believes Putin Seeks Ukraine Deal More Than Zelensky, Urges Meeting
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated his belief that Russian President Vladimir Putin desires a peace deal in Ukraine more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Trump urged both leaders to meet and negotiate, suggesting the US would facilitate an agreement. He also mentioned brokering a diesel deal with Russia for global benefit.

item.title: New Tashkent Opens Doors for Investors and Residents with New Projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited New Tashkent, overseeing the launch of new facilities and construction starts. The city's development, initiated three years ago, is a major urban project. The first phase includes $50 billion in projects, aiming for 2,000 hectares of green zones and 500 hectares of parks, with 150 million square meters of housing planned.

item.title: EU Imposes Sanctions on Russia-North Korea Cooperation in Arms and Economy
item.description: The EU has imposed sanctions on three individuals and four organizations for supporting North Korea's weapons programs and violating UN restrictions through Russia-DPRK cooperation. Sanctions target North Korean labor in Russia, joint projects, and 'oil-for-weapons' trade, deemed violations of UN Security Council resolutions.

item.title: OIC Delegation Discusses Afghanistan's Situation with Taliban Officials in Kabul
item.description: An Organization of Islamic Cooperation delegation met with senior Taliban officials in Kabul to discuss Afghanistan's political, economic, and humanitarian situation. This was the OIC's sixth visit since the Taliban regained power in August 2021. The OIC's public statement following the talks did not mention restrictions on women and girls.

item.title: Doctor Dies After Interrogation in Akmola Region; Police Launch Investigation
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Akmola region are investigating the death of a 38-year-old therapist who died at home shortly after being questioned as a witness in a criminal case. The doctor, who had recently returned from vacation, reportedly had her phone confiscated during the interrogation. Authorities are investigating the case as incitement to suicide, but a link between the interrogation and her death has not yet been established.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Expand Palliative Care and Rehabilitation Services for Children
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a national plan aiming to provide palliative care and rehabilitation services to 90% of children with oncological and hematological diseases by 2035. Currently, only 2-3% of the estimated 35,000 children needing such care receive it. The plan includes establishing specialized palliative care units in all regions and mobile teams for home-based care.

item.title: Khorezm Region Allocates 1 Billion Sums for Women's Entrepreneurship Development
item.description: The Khorezm region has allocated 1 billion sums in grants to support the business initiatives of 25 women as part of the 'Rural Entrepreneurship Development' project. The project, in collaboration with the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction and the World Bank, aims to boost rural entrepreneurship and income generation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Leaders Hold Phone Conversation
item.description: The leaders of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan held a phone conversation, discussing the successful chairmanship of Turkmenistan in regional meetings and the strengthening of bilateral strategic partnership. They emphasized expanding trade, industrial cooperation, and joint projects in energy, transport, and agriculture, as well as cultural exchanges.

item.title: Restaurant Owner in Aktobe Region Pays $200,000 Tenge for Food Poisoning Incident
item.description: A restaurant owner in Kandyagash, Aktobe region, has been ordered to pay 200,000 tenge in moral damages to a guest who suffered food poisoning. The guest was among 188 people affected by an outbreak at the "Tumar" restaurant. The restaurant was operating without a permit, and food samples revealed infectious agents.

item.title: Taliban's Rule Creates More Opponents Than Supporters, Alienating Ideological Allies
item.description: The Taliban's governance is reportedly multiplying opponents by alienating even those with shared ideological foundations. Figures like Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, despite a history of Islamist politics, are now challenging the Taliban's legitimacy and methods. This suggests a "repulsive force" stemming from ethnic power monopolies and refusal to accept Afghanistan's pluralism.

item.title: Taliban Detain 13 Workers in Parwan; Whereabouts Unknown After 26 Days
item.description: Local sources in Parwan province report that 13 workers were detained by the Taliban 26 days ago in Hanrowa Bala village. Their current whereabouts remain unknown, and local officials have provided no clear information despite inquiries from community elders and representatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Foreign Ministries Agree on Three-Year Cooperation Plan
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium's foreign ministries have signed a cooperation roadmap for 2027-2029. The plan aims to boost political dialogue, inter-agency contacts, and joint initiatives. The agreement was reached in Astana during a meeting between Kazakh Deputy Foreign Minister Yerzhan Ashikbayev and Belgian official Theodora Gentzis.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Enhance State Procurement System Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan is set to improve its state procurement system as part of reforms aimed at fostering competition and efficient budget spending. Changes to the Law "On State Procurement" are planned, focusing on removing local producer preferences, increasing transparency, and strengthening parliamentary oversight. Regional complaint commissions will also be established.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Deputy Prime Minister Emphasizes Practical Solutions to Educational Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education and Science, Erkinjon Turdimov, stressed the need for practical solutions rather than just listing problems. During a meeting with ministry staff, discussions focused on expanding preschool education, improving school quality, youth career guidance, and fostering interest in science. Key tasks include raising the teacher's status and creating better conditions for educators.

item.title: Almaty Police Warn of 'Trap Date' Robbery Scheme Targeting Young Men
item.description: Almaty police have identified and prosecuted four groups involved in a 'trap date' robbery scheme this year. The modus operandi involves women meeting men online, luring them to apartments where accomplices pose as relatives to extort money and rob victims. Authorities urge caution with online acquaintances and advise immediate reporting of threats.

item.title: Dogs from Shelter Whose Owner Was Murdered Relocated in Almaty Region
item.description: Dogs from the 'Tvardovsky Dom' shelter, whose owner Vladimir Teplyakov was murdered, have been moved to a new location. Volunteers from the 'Dvoryanskoye Sobraniye' shelter in Almaty facilitated the relocation, citing immense effort and cost. The dogs are now safe and cared for, but the search for new homes continues, requiring financial aid and public support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth Faces Challenges in Tax System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan boasts the fastest-growing economy in the EAEU, with GDP increasing by 11.1% in 2025. Despite favorable tax rates and business conditions, the country's tax administration system presents challenges. Tax revenues grew significantly in the first nine months of 2026, but underlying issues may hinder predictable business growth.

item.title: Concert Organizer Faces Five Years in Prison for Shymkent Stampede
item.description: An investigation is ongoing into a mass stampede at a Kairat Nurtas concert in Shymkent. The organizer has been detained and faces charges of violating safety requirements. Penalties could include a fine of up to 5,000 MCI or imprisonment for up to five years. An 18-year-old girl remains in serious condition.

item.title: Nobel Prize in Economics Awarded for Work on Inflation Control and Crisis Mitigation
item.description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics to American economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford for their work on the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization. Their research has significantly improved governments' and central banks' ability to implement stabilization policies, aiding in controlling inflation and preventing overheating.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks Pakistan's Help Amid Depleting Air Defense Missiles Against Houthi Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia has requested military assistance from Pakistan to defend against Houthi attacks, as the Kingdom's air defense missile supplies are reportedly running low. The United States is not providing the requested military aid to the Saudi prince. This situation highlights the kingdom's vulnerability in its ongoing conflict.

item.title: Pakistan Claims Over 20,000 Terrorists, Including TTP Members, Sheltering in Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's Information Minister stated that over 20,000 terrorists, including 6,000 TTP members, are harbored in Afghanistan. He alleged these individuals receive training in safe havens on Afghan territory and urged the Taliban to prevent terrorist activities, a claim denied by Taliban officials.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region. Previously, he served as the head of the Department for Public Security and Rule of Law within the Presidential Administration. This appointment follows the previous governor's transition to a new role as First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Baxtiyorovich Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region, as announced by presidential press secretary Sherzod Asadov. Qodirov previously headed the Presidential Administration's Department for Public Security and Rule of Law since July 2025. Before that, he served as an advisor on coordinating law enforcement activities.

item.title: Botir Kudratkhodjayev Appointed New Defense Minister of Uzbekistan
item.description: Botir Kudratkhodjayev has been appointed as the new Defense Minister of Uzbekistan by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Kudratkhodjayev, a Major General, previously served as the First Deputy Interior Minister. He also led the Ministry of Emergency Situations and held various prosecutor positions before his current appointment, replacing Lieutenant General Shuhrat Kholmukhamedov.

item.title: Kremlin Rejects Ukraine's 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal for Elections
item.description: The Kremlin has rejected Ukraine's proposal for a 60-day ceasefire to hold presidential elections, stating it would allow Ukraine to regroup for further conflict. Russia might consider a one-day pause only on the election day itself, if elections are scheduled. Ukraine previously suggested this for campaign and voting conditions.
